diagnosis.message: Hello! Today we learn REST design. If you were building an API for student records, what addresses would you create?

explain.message: Think of a library register. The register is about one thing, books. You can look up books, add a book, update a book, or remove a book. REST designs an API the same way. The URL names the thing, a noun like /students, never a verb like /getStudents. The HTTP method says the action: GET reads, POST creates, PUT or PATCH updates, DELETE removes. Status codes say what happened: 200 ok, 201 created, 404 not found. Every request carries all it needs; the server does not remember earlier ones. Shall we design student records?
explain.code:
GET    /students          list students
GET    /students/42       one student
POST   /students          add a student      → 201
PUT    /students/42       replace student 42
PATCH  /students/42       change some fields
DELETE /students/42       remove student 42  → 204
explain.mermaid:
graph TD
  R[/students resource/] --> G[GET read]
  R --> P[POST create]
  R --> U[PUT or PATCH update]
  R --> D[DELETE remove]

example.message: For student records: GET /students lists them, GET /students/42 gets one, POST /students adds one and returns 201, PATCH /students/42 changes a phone number, DELETE /students/42 removes one and returns 204. Why is /deleteStudent?id=42 a poor design?

another_way.message: Another way: a ration shop register. The register is for families. Look up a family, add a family, change a family's card, close a card. The register stays the same; only the action changes. In REST, which part of the request carries the action?

doubt.answer: Good question. PUT replaces the whole record, PATCH changes only some fields. To update just a phone number, PATCH is the better fit. Does that help?

questions: Design REST endpoints for a {context}: list, read one, add, update and delete. Explain the methods and status codes.
An API for a {context} has URLs like /getAll and /deleteItem. Explain what is wrong and how REST would fix it.
Explain the difference between PUT and PATCH, and when you would use 201 and 404, for a {context}.

feedback.missing: Add the status codes each endpoint returns.
